page.layout: One column of text, centred on the page, followed by the closing lines (date, year and signature) below it. No running head, page number or margin notes. A printed ornament (asterisks) sits between the date and the signature.

main_text.p: omnia in te agnoui : nunquam ab eo destiti silentio,atque ἐυφη-[?]μία animum istum tuum tam excelsum , & tot virtutibus exaggeratum venerari. cuius affectus, animíque in te mei patere obsecro te , vir maxime , extare hoc , cuicuimodi est , testimonium : meámque hanc sive temeritatem, sive audaciam æqui boni consule. Vale. à d.

page.notes: The ornament between the date and the signature is a printer's asterisk device and is not transcribed. The Greek word split at the line end reads ἐυφη- / μία (εὐφημία); the breathing and accent on the first syllable are hard to make out at this scan resolution. Long s has been normalised to s throughout (e.g. "filentio", "destiti", "obsecro", "sive"), so the printed f-like glyphs are rendered as s. The date "CIↃ. IↃ. XCII." is the old reversed-C form and is given as MDXCII. "PET." is the signature of the letter and is left as printed.
